# ZX Spectrum 48K platforms

The installed toolchain contains two assembly-backed Spectrum platforms:

| Platform | Output | Runtime address |
|---|---|---|
| `zx-ram` | Fixed-address flat binary, optionally packaged as TAP/TZX | `0x5CCB` |
| `zx-rom` | Exact 16 KiB replacement ROM | `0x0000` |

## RAM and tape

```sh
xcc -Os --platform=zx-ram --oformat=binary main.c -o app.bin
xprog --tap app.bin -o app.tap --name APP
xprog --tzx app.bin -o app.tzx --name APP
```

At a standard 48K BASIC prompt, load either tape with `LOAD ""`. The generated
BASIC bootstrap uses the Sinclair ROM loader but permits the CODE block to
overwrite it, so the program can genuinely begin at the lowest practical RAM
address, `0x5CCB`.

## Replacement ROM

```sh
xcc -Os --platform=zx-rom --oformat=binary main.c -o app.rom
```

The output covers `0x0000`–`0x3FFF` and includes reset, RST, interrupt, and NMI
vectors. Writable storage begins at `0x5B00`; startup copies initialized data
from its packed ROM load image, clears BSS, initializes the console, and calls
`main`.

## Runtime services

Both targets expose non-blocking `kbhit()` from `<conio.h>`. On ZX it
returns the current mapped ASCII key, or zero when no key is down. Blocking
keyboard-matrix `stdin` is implemented by looping around the same poller.
Bitmap `stdout`/`stderr` use a YOS-derived renderer and a proportional 6x12
Tamsyn font exported by snatch, with CR/LF, pixel-granular wrapping, 16 rows,
and 12-pixel scrolling.

There is no filesystem or wall clock. File descriptors above 2 and file-backed
stdio operations fail; `gettimeofday`/`settimeofday` fail; `time`, `clock`, and
`timespec_get` propagate the standard no-clock result. Allocation, strings,
conversions, formatted console I/O, sorting/searching, math, and compiler
runtime operations use the normal assembly libc.

The heap extends from the linked writable image to `0xEFFF`. `0xF000`–`0xFFFF`
is reserved for the descending stack. `exit` records `zx_exit_status` and
enters a permanent interrupt-disabled HALT loop.

## Fuse

```sh
fuse --machine 48 --auto-load --tape app.tap
fuse --machine 48 --rom-48 app.rom
```

See `XCC.md`, `XLD.md`, and `XPROG.md` in this directory for the compiler,
ROM load-address, and tape-packaging switches.
